title: POC Weekly Sync - Onboarding & Env Readiness
summary: Weekly POC sync to review onboarding progress, confirm access to VPC and GPU targets, review initial latency/cost numbers, and plan next steps for benchmark runs. Customer needs KMS integration and SOC2 docs before expanding dedicated capacity evaluation.
next_steps: Redwood to send SOC2 and network architecture doc (Jordan, by 2025-10-17)
Priya to run a focused 90m benchmark on 2x A100-equivalent nodes and share results (Priya, by 2025-10-20)
Customer to provide service account + VPC peering details and firewall rules (Samir, by 2025-10-17)
Schedule live demo of private deployment options if benchmarks look good (Jordan + Marta, tentative week of 2025-10-27)
action_items: Samir Patel: Provide VPC peering CIDR, service account, and firewall egress ports; due 2025-10-17
Priya Patel (Redwood SE): Run 90m benchmark with kv-cache enabled and share raw logs; due 2025-10-20
Jordan Lee (AE): Share SOC2 report, KMS integration guide, and pricing estimate; due 2025-10-17
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-10-15 16:00 UTC
Duration: 00:45:00
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (BlueWave - Head of ML), Samir Patel (BlueWave - DevOps), Oliver Chen (BlueWave - Product)

Auto-summary (may be imperfect): Quick sync; onboarding progressing; need peering + KMS; plan benchmarks; send SOC2.

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on, we'll keep this to about 45 minutes. quick roll call? 
[00:08] Marta Ruiz: Hi, Marta here, thanks. 
[00:11] Samir Patel: Samir here, DevOps. 
[00:14] Oliver Chen: Oliver, product. 
[00:16] Priya Patel: Priya from Redwood, SE. 
[00:18] Jordan Lee: Great. Agenda — access & VPC, readiness for benchmark, security docs, next steps.

[00:30] Jordan Lee: Samir, last week you mentioned you had a service account almost ready and were waiting on firewall rules — where are we? 
[00:38] Samir Patel: Yeah, we got the service account, just need to finalize the egress rules. I have the list but I wanted to confirm the outbound IPs from Redwood, we have some corporate policy around static IP allowlists. 
[00:52] Jordan Lee: Right — for the Hosted path we use range X, but for Private we do VPC peering so IPs aren't a thing. For Dedicated, we can provide fixed egress if needed or use customer NAT. I'll attach the IP ranges in the notes. 
[01:08] Samir Patel: Ok that helps, but for the initial benchmark we were hoping to do it over our test VPC via peering — ping times are important. 

[01:22] Priya Patel: From the SE side I'm mostly focused on the runtime config — which model family are you testing again? 
[01:28] Marta Ruiz: We're doing an open model, LLaMA-2-70B-ish quantized, and some custom reranker. Latency target is sub-300ms p90 for 1k token prompts in our critical path. 
[01:42] Priya Patel: Got it. For that profile we'll enable kv-cache and set batching minimal. Also we'll set compilation flags to prefer int8 kernels. There might be a small quality delta with quantization — have you got a short eval set? 
[01:58] Marta Ruiz: Yes, I shared a 200 prompt eval set in the drive link — the one labeled 'bluewave_eval_v1'. 
[02:04] Jordan Lee: Perfect, Priya can run the eval during the benchmark run. For the p90 target we should be able to hit it on a 2x A100-equivalent pool with the right kernel selection and prefix caching but we'll verify.

[02:22] Samir Patel: About KMS — we have a corporate requirement that customer keys can't leave our cloud. Does Redwood support customer-managed KMS for Private? 
[02:30] Jordan Lee: Yes, for Private we integrate with customer KMS/HSM. For Dedicated we offer KMS integration as an option. I'll send the KMS integration guide and the SOC2 artifacts after the call. 
[02:42] Samir Patel: Good; also need to confirm retention — logs and request payloads, retention default and how to disable retention. 
[02:49] Priya Patel: We can set retention policies; for the POC we can turn off request logging to minimize data persistence. We'll note that in the runbook. 

[03:05] Oliver Chen: Any known blockers on the Redwood side for getting the benchmark running? 
[03:09] Priya Patel: Not really — once we have the peering and service account we'll trigger a 90-minute focused run. I might ask to bump up connection timeout on your side for long prompts. 
[03:18] Marta Ruiz: Also curious about observability — will we get per-token latency breakdown and token cost? 
[03:24] Jordan Lee: Yes, Redwood Console gives token-level cost and latency, per-route dashboards and traces. We'll share a sample dashboard link. 

[03:35] [silence / typing]

[03:48] Priya Patel: Quick note — for the quantized model we may recommend enabling a small batch size with continous batching; odd though, but it increases throughput without hitting latency SLOs. We'll test both. 
[04:02] Marta Ruiz: Ok. On timeline — we hope to decide on Dedicated vs Hosted by mid-November; this POC is gating that. 
[04:10] Jordan Lee: Understood. Can we agree milestones — networking by Friday, benchmark run next week, deliverables and pricing by the 20th? 
[04:20] Samir Patel: Yes that's doable. 
[04:22] Jordan Lee: Awesome. Any other questions? 
[04:25] Oliver Chen: Nothing from product. 
[04:27] Marta Ruiz: No.

[04:30] Jordan Lee: Recap and owners — I'll send SOC2, KMS guide, and IP ranges (Jordan, due 2025-10-17). Priya will run benchmark (Priya, due 2025-10-20). Samir to share peering details (Samir, due 2025-10-17). We'll tentatively book a private deployment demo week of 2025-10-27 if results are promising.

[04:50] Jordan Lee: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links to the runbook and the shared artifacts. 
[04:55] Marta Ruiz: Thanks, bye.
